composing_units: 1st Infantry Division; 29th Infantry Division; attached: 2nd and 5th Ranger Battalions
engaged_with: German 352nd Infantry Division; German 716th Static Infantry Division
notes: Assault corps at Omaha (Gerow); ~34,250 men landed D-Day. Beachhead only shallow by nightfall.

location_name: Forêt de Cerisy / Caumont gap sector
composing_units: 1st Infantry Division; 2nd Infantry Division; 29th Infantry Division; 2nd Armored Division (less CCA, in reserve)
current_activity: attacking toward Saint-Lô with three divisions
notes: Three-division attack 9–13 June after 352nd Division withdrew to the Elle line; 2nd Div reached objectives west/south of the Forêt de Cerisy on 10 June.

current_activity: halting attack toward Saint-Lô; holding Caumont-Carentan line
notes: Attack toward Saint-Lô halted 13 June; line echeloned from Caumont (held by 1st Div) to Carentan. XIX Corps took 29th Div on 14 June.
V Corps went on the defensive in front of Saint-Lô on 18 June; positions held for next two weeks; 3rd Armored Division limited attack 29 June.

composing_units: 2nd Infantry Division; 5th Infantry Division; 35th Infantry Division (attached)
current_activity: taking control of the 35th Division and the front east of the Vire
notes: Event date: Breakout-15 p285 (evening of 27 July Bradley decided to displace XIX Corps west of the Vire, attached the 35th Division to V Corps and extended Gerow's responsibility to the river) and p289 (V Corps took control of the 35th on 28 July). Event definition: V Corps assumes all American-held ground east of the Vire with the 2nd, 5th and 35th Divisions; it secured the Saint-Jean-des-Baisants ridge that day. Relationship: First Army assigned; the 35th is attached to V Corps (see C0425). Location: ridge sector, not the corps command post; the CMH command-post list (World War II by Day) has V Corps at Balleroy from 21 July and Saint-Amand from 8 August. Event support: high (Green Book, dated to the day). Location support: low (sector, not the command post).

current_activity: taking three divisions near Argentan; command post at Alençon
notes: Event date: Breakout-27 p529: by daybreak 17 August Gerow was in the Argentan area, set up a command post in the Hôtel de France at Alençon and took command of three divisions to close the Argentan-Falaise gap; the provisional corps under Gaffey was disbanded; V Corps Artillery moved from Tinchebray to Argentan the same day. Event definition: V Corps replaces the provisional corps in the Argentan sector. Location: Alençon town centroid for the hotel. Relationship: the army boundary was shifted to put Trun and Chambois in the First Army zone; V Corps stays assigned to First Army. Event support: moderate (CMH list and Green Book, date approximate). Location support: high (command post, same day).

current_activity: securing Paris after the German garrison surrendered
notes: Breakout-29 p624: Gerow held military responsibility for Paris, judging it secure on 28 August. Point is the city; the corps command post is not given.

composing_units: 4th Infantry Division; 28th Infantry Division; 5th Armored Division; 102nd Cavalry Group
current_activity: 5th Armored patrol crosses into Germany near Stalzemburg; corps holds 4th, 28th Divisions
notes: Siegfried-1: a Troop B, 85th Cavalry Reconnaissance Squadron patrol crossed the Our near Stalzemburg at 1805 on 11 September, the first onto German soil. Siegfried-2 p23: on 11 September V Corps controlled the 102nd Cavalry Group, 4th and 28th Infantry Divisions and 5th Armored Division. Point is Vianden, a few miles away.
